title: Tailored cover letter from role and resume notes
objective: Measure whether the cover-letter craftbook maps role requirements to real candidate proof points before drafting a tailored letter.
prompt: In the `Cover Letter Eval` project, read `source/job.md` and `source/resume-notes.md`, then write `cover-letter.md` for Avery Chen applying to Operations Automation Manager at Harbor & Finch. The letter must be tailored, one page, cite three concrete proof points, map them to role requirements, include a company hook, and avoid generic filler.

setup.about: Self-contained eval project for the cover-letter craftbook. Job and resume notes are under workspace/source.
setup.missionObjectives: Produce a tailored one-page cover letter mapping Avery Chen proof points to Harbor & Finch role requirements.

files.content:
# Role: Operations Automation Manager, Harbor & Finch

Requirements: design workflow automations, partner with support and warehouse teams, report operational metrics, lead pilots without disrupting daily work. Company hook: Harbor & Finch is expanding a returns-desk automation pilot after measurable support improvements.

# Avery Chen Resume Notes

- Led a two-warehouse barcode exception pilot that cut manual lookup time by 38%.
- Built weekly exception exports for Finance using SQL and CSV automation.
- Partnered with support leads to reduce duplicate status tickets by 22%.
- Trained 34 warehouse associates on new intake workflows.

success.summary: workspace/cover-letter.md is tailored to the seeded role and candidate evidence with company hook and concrete proof points.

checks.pattern: barcode exception|weekly exception exports|duplicate status tickets

axes.name: structure
axes.description: Layout and hierarchy fit the content; sections are scannable and coherent.

axes.name: grounding
axes.description: Seeded source content is used faithfully — no invented facts or dropped requirements.

axes.name: interactivity
axes.description: Controls and states the page claims to offer actually work.

axes.name: polish
axes.description: Styling is intentional and responsive rather than unstyled or broken.
